jamal_support: FYI cust-Delta reported sudden embedding length change after we applied their pinned model -> they expected 1024 but receiving 1536. Customer noticed during nightly reindex job, large failure rate.
jamal_support: forwarded customer payload and sample response below.
jamal_support: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED\" \n -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-v1-pinned:abc123","input":"test"}'```
jamal_support: sample response (truncated): ```{"data":[{"embedding":[0.001, -0.002, ...], "length":1536}]}```
ingrid_eng: :eyes: do we have request_id or job_id? need a trace to check routing and fallback.
jamal_support: request_id 2026-03-12T02:13:44Z: req_9f8a7c. Customer says it coincided with a maintenance canary.
chiara_sre: quick check: pinned alias redwood-embed-v1-pinned:abc123 currently maps to variant set A -> but I see automatic fallback mapping to redwood-embed-v1-quantized-b on host group due to capacity. That quantized variant has a different projection head (1536).
ingrid_eng: aha — so routing fallback returned a compatible text-gen model but with a different embed head. That would change vector width. Wasn’t the pinned policy supposed to prevent cross-variant substitution?
chiara_sre: pin policy is supposed to prefer pinned variant, but fallback by capacity tier can substitute if strict_pin=false on that customer contract. Looks like their account had strict_pin:false after a migration.
jamal_support: customer swears they didn't change strict pin. They asked for us to remediate ASAP — their search index blew up.
ingrid_eng: immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily block fallback for that alias (force strict pin on routing) 2) advise customer to pause batch reindex and re-run with model they expect 3) provide reindex script to detect and repair mismatched vectors.
chiara_sre: I will flip a routing flag for alias redwood-embed-v1-pinned:abc123 to force pinned variant and add a canary check to avoid capacity thrash. Doing it now. deploy-bot: starting alias update job (job_id: alias-update-4478902).
deploy-bot: alias update succeeded, replicas draining then reattaching.
jamal_support: relayed to customer: tell them to stop reindex job and we'll notify when stable. They asked if there will be data corruption for entries already ingested.
ingrid_eng: vectors already stored with 1536 must be re-ingested or downsampled — can't safely convert. Provide a small script to detect vec length and tag docs for reindex.
jamal_support: shared a short detection snippet with customer: ```python\n# pseudo\nif len(doc['embedding']) != 1024:\n  mark_for_reindex(doc_id)\n```
chiara_sre: follow-up: investigating why quantized-b has 1536 — looks like when we onboarded quantized variant we used an alternate tokenizer+head for better quality; mismatch was not flagged because alias schema lacks embed_dim enforcement.
ingrid_eng: long term: add model manifest check that enforces embedding dim compatibility for pinned aliases and raise alert on variant substitution. Also surface a telemetry metric: alias_embed_dim_mismatch.
chiara_sre: logged ENG ticket ENG-1892 for manifest enforcement and PLAT-402 for customer-facing alias strictness toggle in Console.
jamal_support: customer accepted temporary pause and will schedule reindex overnight once we confirm pinned routing stable. They want rollback option if we see thrash.
chiara_sre: action items: - confirm alias routing stability for 24h - run traffic sweep to ensure no other aliases swapped - push alert to oncall if mismatch rate > 0.5% - publish short KB for Support on detecting embed dim mismatches.
ingrid_eng: I'll review kernel selection logs for quantized-b to ensure no silent changes.
ops-bot: incident-note created: INC-2026-3312 (embed-dim-fallback).
jamal_support: thanks team. I'll keep customer updated and file the reindex template in their ticket. :thumbsup:
